title: 8 major updates to Cloudflare Observability
description: Cloudflare is launching eight major updates that bring logs, traces, analytics, alerts, dashboards, querying, and telemetry export into one observability platform, with simpler and more predictable pricing.

title: Streamline: custom video pipelines with Cloudflare Stream and Workers
description: Streamline demonstrates how to build long-running, continuous video processing pipelines by pairing Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects with a containerized media engine.

title: DNS Spotlight: Silver Fox Strikes Anew with a Fake Installer Campaign
description: A Silver Fox-style fake installer campaign used deceptive software download sites to distribute malware, while DNS and WHOIS analysis uncovered typosquatting domains, potential victim traffic and more than 1,500 campaign-connected artifacts.

title: German Study Finds Industrial AI Driving €120 Billion in Revenue
description: German companies are building an industrial AI advantage by combining existing models with proprietary data and engineering expertise, generating more than EUR 120 billion in revenue from AI-enabled products, according to an IW study.

title: Introducing Web Search API via AI Gateway
description: Cloudflare AI Gateway now supports native web search API integration in partnership with Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. Developers can now inject real-time web context into model inference calls via AI Gateway, REST APIs, or Workers bindings.

title: Introducing Cloudflare Traces: follow requests through our entire platform
description: Cloudflare Traces shows how a request moves through security rules, transformations, cache, routing, Workers, and your origin, then follows it across services running anywhere in your stack.

title: Updates on our pledge to make Cloudflare features accessible to everyone
description: A year after pledging to eliminate two-tier product access, Cloudflare has expanded Logpush, multi-account governance, and higher platform limits to all accounts. Here is an update on our progress, how we dogfood these tools internally, and what is coming next.

title: Announcing Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway – expanding access to Cloudflare’s privacy-preserving infrastructure
description: We’re announcing the closed beta of a self-serve Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway. We’re also renaming our Privacy Gateway to Cloudflare OHTTP Relay to better distinguish the two products.

title: Follow the thread: a new dashboard to investigate account abuse
description: Fraudsters are increasingly using AI to bypass stateless security checks. Cloudflare's new Account Abuse Protection dashboard uses stateful analysis and edge-generated Hashed User IDs to help teams investigate and block account abuse.

title: Protected Quick Tunnels: simple accountless authentication for your next dev project
description: Quick Tunnels now support email authentication. Add --allowed-mail to one cloudflared command, and only the addresses or domains you list can reach your local app. No Cloudflare account required on either side.

title: Building for good: How civil society organizations are automating on Cloudflare
description: Some of the world's leading organizations are building the future of non-profit work with Cloudflare.

title: 2026 Birthday week: network performance update
description: Cloudflare now ranks as the fastest provider across 74% of the top 1,000 global networks. By incorporating background telemetry from Cloudflare Challenge Pages, we have expanded our real-user measurement scale while maintaining user privacy.

title: Is RPKI becoming harmful to BGP stability?
description: Guest Post: Could the growing deployment of RPKI become a threat to routing stability? This study analyses more than 11 years of RPKI and BGP data, measuring how much routing activity can be associated with RPKI-related changes.

title: .si Registrations Surge After US Shift to ‘Super Intelligence’
description: Slovenia's .si domain registrations surged after President Donald Trump promoted "Super Intelligence," with September registrations reaching 46,066 as investors sought names matching the new SI abbreviation.

title: Get Ready for ARIN Elections
description: The 2026 ARIN Elections are approaching, making this a good time to review the process and the participation opportunities available to you and your organization. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you prepare to cast your vote this fall.

title: [Podcast] The October 2026 root KSK roll
description: In this episode of PING, Verisign's Duane Wessels discusses the transition to the third DNS root KSK key pair, which is scheduled to begin signing the root zone on 11 October 2026.

title: New features for RFC-Editor.org
description: New features implemented on RFC-Editor.org aim to make the site more useful and engaging for RFC consumers.

title: AT&T Chief Challenges Economics of SpaceX’s Mobile-Network Strategy
description: AT&T CEO John Stankey questions the economics of SpaceX's expanding mobile strategy as regulatory filings and independent measurements show the spectrum, satellite capacity and terrestrial infrastructure involved in scaling direct-to-device service.

title: ICANN Sets October 7 for 2026 New gTLD Reveal Day
description: ICANN will publish applicants, proposed strings and initial contention sets for the 2026 new gTLD round on October 7, followed by a replacement-string period and final string confirmation on November 17.

title: Opinion: The economics of AI
description: As spending on data centres, power, and computing capacity surges, the question is no longer whether AI delivers value, but who will ultimately pay for it.

title: AI-driven networking and infrastructure design at APNIC 62
description: Presenters at APNIC 62 explored how AI is reshaping network design and operations, from next-generation optical architectures to autonomous management systems, highlighting scale challenges and improved reliability, efficiency, and operational decision-making.

title: OpenAI Agent Bypasses Internet Restrictions Through DNS
description: OpenAI paused tool-enabled work on its most capable models after a research agent bypassed sandbox Internet restrictions by using DNS to communicate with an external chatbot during reinforcement-learning training.

title: The Economics Behind AI’s Infrastructure Boom
description: AI's infrastructure boom is consuming vast amounts of capital, power and computing hardware, raising questions about whether advertising, subscriptions and corporate spending can ultimately support the industry's expanding cost base.

title: SpaceX Deploys First 26 Starlink V3 Satellites on Starship
description: SpaceX deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites on Starship’s first orbital mission, beginning a network expansion whose promised capacity gains depend on the spacecraft completing checkout and entering service.

title: Restricting the Acquisition of Additional LIR Accounts
description: The RIPE NCC Executive Board has decided to temporarily restrict members' ability to acquire additional Local Internet Registry (LIR) accounts. Taking effect on Tuesday, 29 September, the restriction also covers requests already in progress. The decision is a first step towards a…

title: ARIN Bits: September 2026
description: The days may be shortening as we enter fall at ARIN HQ in Virginia, but we’re not slowing down the steady pace of changes, upgrades, and outreach that cropped up throughout July, August, and September. We’ve gathered the season’s key developments and upcoming opportunities in thi…

title: Thou shall not pass: Gatekeeping outbound TLS connections
description: Guest Post: To quantify how closely guideline recommendations align with real-world TLS deployments, we collected over 50 million TLS handshakes during two weeks from our research institution.

title: Africa Is Adopting AI but Who Is Governing the Risks?
description: African institutions are adopting AI across public services and business, but effective deployment requires governance structures that address cybersecurity, accountability, procurement, digital sovereignty, regulatory coordination and institutional capacity.

title: SpaceX Wants to End Rural Broadband Subsidies
description: SpaceX argues that Starlink makes rural broadband subsidies obsolete, but questions about speed, universal availability, voice service and affordability complicate its case for eliminating high-cost Universal Service Fund support.

title: Apply now for an APRICOT 2027 Fellowship
description: APRICOT is offering a limited number of fellowships in the lead up to APRICOT 2027. Apply now!

title: APNIC 62 Policy SIG reviews seven policy proposals, with two reaching consensus
description: APNIC 62 Policy SIG discussed seven proposals covering IPv4, IPv6, and Internet abuse-related issues.

title: IP geolocation at APNIC 62: Challenges, geofeeds, and data quality perspectives
description: At APNIC 62, panellists explored how geofeeds, RIR data, and third-party geolocation providers work together, and why improving accuracy while protecting user privacy is becoming increasingly important.

title: Meet the 2026 ARIN Community Grant Recipients
description: We would like to congratulate the organizations receiving funding from the ARIN Community Grant Program this year! Senior Project Manager Amanda Gauldin shares details about their projects.

title: PeeringDB Update April - September 2026
description: The last six months has seen important improvements to PeeringDB. We've added in page maps for searches of interconnection facilities and improved the data quality for AS-SET names.

title: Understanding ASPA: The next step in routing security
description: Join this APNIC Academy webinar to understand how ASPAs work, how they complement ROAs, and how you can begin monitoring and deploying them in your network.

title: The RIPE Chair Team Reports - September 2026
description: With RIPE 93 fast approaching, the RIPE Chair Team shares updates on policy and Working Group activity, the Code of Conduct Team document, and recent events across the Internet community.

title: Moving to a New Board Structure
description: A governance structure is strongest when the responsibilities written down on paper match the responsibilities exercised in practice. This proposal to change the RIPE NCC’s governance structure is intended to make sure that they do.

title: Latest BGP hijack targets hosting software vendor
description: Guest Post: An analysis of the BGP hijack against Softaculous that enabled an attacker to obtain a fraudulent TLS certificate and distribute a malicious Virtualizor update.

title: CAPIF 5: Regional Interconnectivity in Central Asia
description: Central Asia’s Internet looks very different than it did back at CAPIF 1. We trace the rise of direct regional routes, stronger routing security and new connectivity options - along with the gaps that remain.

title: IETF email infrastructure transition completed on 11 September
description: A transition to a new modern, modular, and containerized infrastructure for email services provided for ietf.org, iab.org, irtf.org, rfc-editor.org (including email lists) was completed on 11 September 2026.

title: The /3 Body Problem
description: A large chunk of IPv6 is heading for space, and every policy question about it is currently going to be deferred to the RIR communities. This article outlines what those questions look like, and argues why now is the time to start asking them.

title: Survey to gather input on ISE selection criteria
description: The Independent Series Editor (ISE) selection criteria survey is live and we welcome your input on the capabilities and expectations the IAB should consider when selecting a future ISE. Please respond by 11 October 2026.

title: The Internet’s New Edge Builders
description: After building private backbones, content and cloud platforms are now moving closer to users. In doing so, they are taking on delivery roles once associated mainly with independent CDNs.

title: Closing the IPv6 First-Packet Gap with GRAND
description: There is a subtle asymmetry in IPv6 Neighbour Discovery: a host knows how to reach its router before the router necessarily knows how to reach the host. GRAND fixes that asymmetry by making the host proactively advertise its address, and I implemented that mechanism in FreeBSD.

title: Introducing the ARIN 58 Fellows
description: Amanda Gauldin, ARIN Senior Project Manager, shares details about the Fellows, Mentors, and special guests joining us for the ARIN 58 Fellowship Program.

title: When Traceroutes Lie: How TTL Jumps Can Give Us a False Impression of the Internet’s Topology
description: Traceroute is a powerful tool for uncovering how packets travel across the Internet. However, as we recently discovered, some routers tamper with the TTL values in traceroute's probing packets, giving you a false view of how networks are actually interconnected.

title: Spurs boots VMware, cites 85% licensing saving
description: Part of wider infrastructure replacement upgrade project with HPE

title: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice in Internet Operations
description: Internet research can benefit from operational insight, and network operators from research expertise. Building on what we learned at RIPE 92, we look at practical ways to make those connections easier and turn promising conversations into lasting collaboration.

title: IETF 126 Highlights
description: The IETF 126 meeting was held 18–24 July 2026 at the Hilton Vienna Park in Vienna, Austria, and online, hosted by Cisco. The week included the IETF Hackathon and Code Sprint, the New Participants' Program, five Birds-of-a-Feather (BoF) sessions, and more than 100 working group an…

title: Post-Quantum Authentication: Up Next
description: Post-quantum key establishment has moved from standards into deployment. Post-quantum authentication has not moved nearly as far, and specification work is no longer the only constraint. The IAB is holding a workshop in Prague on 11 and 12 October 2026 to bring deployment experie…

title: IETF 126 post-meeting survey: what we heard
description: The IETF 126 Vienna meeting was held 18-24 July 2026 and the results of the post-meeting survey are now available.

title: Make the Switch to More Secure API Key Handling for Reg-RWS
description: ARIN now supports sending your Reg-RWS API key through a header instead of a URL query parameter — a small change that closes off a real source of accidental credential exposure. Here's why it matters and how to make the switch.

title: Meet our new IETF NOC Lead
description: Joe Clarke has been appointed as the new IETF Network Operations Center (NOC) Lead and in this post Joe introduces himself and sets out his priorities for the IETF Network.

title: The State of IPv6 in the Caribbean
description: It's time for our annual update on who’s leading the charge for IPv6 adoption in the Caribbean, featuring new leaders and new lessons emerging from this year’s data.

title: Your Number Resource Record Is a Part of the Internet's Infrastructure — Respect It Like One
description: Legacy IPv4 Internet number resource holders: Is your registration data still doing its job? Nearly half of ARIN's legacy networks have no validated Point of Contact. Find out why that matters, and how to fix it in minutes.

title: Secretariat restructuring and staffing update
description: There have been a few changes in IETF Administration LLC staffing since January of this year (2026) including the recent insourcing of the Secretariat, which are summarised here to give an overall view of the staffing structure.

title: Don’t Get Your Wires Crossed: Appropriate Use Cases for IPv6-Only vs. IPv6-Mostly
description: Terms like IPv6-only and IPv6-mostly are a clear example of how IETF terminology often lacks clarity. IPv6 expert Jordi Palet Martínez, explains why the correct use of these terms requires specifying a scope of application.

title: IETF Community Survey 2025
description: The IETF Community Survey provides a comprehensive assessment of community demographics, engagement patterns, and perceptions of organizational effectiveness. Read the full findings below.

title: Apply Today for the ARIN 58 Fellowship Program
description: The call for applications to our ARIN 58 Fellowship Program is out, and Senior Project Manager Amanda Gauldin shares more about what you can expect in this program, why you should consider applying, and what past Fellows have to say about the experience.

title: Birds of a Feather at IETF 126
description: The IETF 126 Vienna meeting takes place 18–24 July 2026. As at every IETF meeting, alongside the established Working Groups there will be a handful of Birds-of-a-Feather (BoF) sessions—and these are often the most interesting place to watch where Internet standards work is headin…
